notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase. The Sanskrit and the other Chinese/Tibetan versions give different numbers of vows (e.g. 24, 36, 46, 49).

paraphrase: The eighteenth vow: 'If, when I attain buddhahood, beings of the ten directions who sincerely and joyfully entrust themselves, wish to be born in my land and think of me even ten times, should not be born there, may I not attain perfect awakening — excepting those who commit the five grave offences and slander the true dharma.'

paraphrase: Three grades of those who aspire to Sukhāvatī: the highest renounce the household, arouse the thought of awakening, single-mindedly think of Amitāyus and cultivate merit; the middle, unable to renounce, still arouse the thought of awakening and do good; the lowest, who can do no merit, arouse the thought of awakening and single-mindedly think of him even ten times; all are welcomed at death.

paraphrase: One cannot be born in that land with few good roots and little merit: a good man or woman who hears of Amitābha and holds fast to his name for one day, or up to seven days, with a mind undistracted, will see Amitābha and the holy assembly before them at the end of life, and dying without confusion will be born in Sukhāvatī.

paraphrase: Sixteen contemplations taught to Vaidehī: (1) the setting sun, (2) water becoming ice and lapis ground, (3) the ground, (4) the jewel trees, (5) the ponds, (6) the jewel towers, (7) the lotus throne, (8) the images of the Buddha and bodhisattvas, (9) the true body of Amitāyus, (10) Avalokiteśvara, (11) Mahāsthāmaprāpta, (12) oneself born in a lotus there, (13) the mixed contemplation of the small and great bodies.
